description:
UMBRELLA for the HTR-10 thermal-spectrum critical path. Audit 2026-08-11.

QUESTION ANSWERED: yes, njoy-outram-park-fork is the correct owner of S(alpha,beta) — root CLAUDE.md puts all cross-section/nuclear-data code there and keeps transport crates data-free, and the code already follows that (thermr reads MF=7; outram-mc-libs holds no ENDF parsing and builds its ThermalScattering from the njoy surface).

WHAT ALREADY WORKS (verified by running the port against ENDF/B-VIII.0, not by reading docs):
  - MF=7 parsing of all three graphite evaluations: tsl-crystalline-graphite (MAT=30), tsl-reactor-graphite-10P (MAT=31), -30P (MAT=32). All report coherent_elastic=true, incoherent_elastic=false, incoherent_inelastic=true.
  - Coherent-elastic sigma(E) with correct physics: zero below the Bragg cutoff, first edge at 1.83e-3 eV (graphite (002)), 24 open reflections at 0.0253 eV, sigma_coh_el(0.0253) = 4.55 b.
  - Incoherent-inelastic sigma_inel(E) reaching the free-atom limit (4.61 b at 3.9 eV vs B(1) = 4.739 b), and a 16-bin equiprobable emission table.
  - THERMR is REAL, not a scaffold: coherent, incoherent-elastic and incoherent-inelastic all implemented (~1.4k lines across src/thermr/). Only thermr::run(), the NJOY card-input driver, is NotPorted — the typed module API is the intended entry point.

DATA IS AVAILABLE OFFLINE: /home/teddy0/Documents/research/ENDF-B-VIII.0/thermal_scatt/ holds all three graphite tapes plus their .leapr decks and .readme provenance. reference-data/endf/ in-repo holds only a README (no tapes). LEAPR is therefore NOT on the critical path — the S(alpha,beta) already exists and does not need generating.

THE GAP IS THE LAST MILE, AND IT IS TOTAL: crates/outram-mc-libs/src/pebble_beds/ has ZERO references to thermal scattering (grep for thermal/ThermalScattering/with_thermal returns nothing across delta_tracking.rs, keff_delta.rs, mod.rs, sphere_packing.rs). The pebble-bed graphite matrix is currently pure free-gas.

ORDERED BLOCKERS:
  1. op-h23 — carbon in well_known_mat. DONE 2026-08-11 (C-12 MAT=625, C-13 MAT=628, verified against the tapes).
  2. op-1y4y — coherent-elastic extra-temperature S(E) tables are discarded; sigma_coh_el only at 296 K. Hard blocker for the 120/250 C benchmark points and all hot operation.
  3. op-u5ju — njoy consumer surface for the elastic channels.
  4. op-nhoa — outram-mc ThermalScattering elastic channel + sampling.
  5. THIS BEAD — wire it into pebble_beds material construction and add an HTR-10 graphite thermal-spectrum V&V case.

Also relevant: op-cjw.22 (inelastic temperature interpolation) is filed P4 on the stated assumption that 'target temps (293.6K) are tabulated exactly'. That assumption FAILS for HTR-10: requested 393 K and 523 K snap to tabulated 400 K and 500 K, a 23 K error at the 250 C point. Consider re-prioritising.

DO NOT describe HTR-10 neutronics as validated until this closes.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content:
STEP 5 DONE 2026-08-14 -- the pebble-bed wiring, the majorant re-check, and the end-to-end number this bead demanded all now exist and are measured.

WHAT THE 'MOSTLY CLOSED' CLAIM MISSED. Commit e4afd51779 added tests/htr10_graphite_thermal_scattering_pebble_bed.rs and described it as closing most of this bead, but its k-eigenvalue test was #[ignore]d and therefore never ran. Un-ignoring it exposed TWO real defects:

1. THE STATED BLOCKER WAS NOT REAL. The ignore reason was that Nuclide::from_core("C12") fails with WmpData("nuclide C12 not in WMPL container"), attributed to a gap in the embedded WMPL blob and filed as op-wqk.21 (which was never actually created -- it is absent from the store). There is no data gap: the CORE library carries natural carbon as "C0" (ENDF/B-VII.1 ZA 006000, listed as 'C-nat | 006000' in wmp-nuclide-manifest.md). tests/thermal_graphite_elastic.rs:307 already used "C0" correctly. It was a wrong nuclide name, not missing data. No op-wqk.21 is needed.

2. THE ACTUAL WIRING DEFECT, which the ignored test was hiding. With C0 in place the free-gas and bound runs returned BIT-IDENTICAL k. Root cause: Nuclide::sample_thermal had exactly ONE caller in the crate, physics::transport_csg. Neither physics::keff (collide_batched, transport_history, transport_history_tabulated) nor pebble_beds::keff_delta called it. So xs_at_energy correctly substituted the BOUND cross section -- setting collision rates -- while secondary energy and angle were still drawn free-gas. Internally inconsistent, and it admits no up-scatter, so a graphite-moderated spectrum cannot equilibrate. All five collision sites now route through the bound-atom law below the table cutoff, mirroring transport_csg / OpenMC src/thermal.cpp ThermalData::sample. sample_thermal consumes no RNG when there is no table or the neutron is above cutoff, so every non-thermal nuclide is bit-identical -- full suite 265 passed / 0 failed confirms no regression.

3. THE TEST PROBLEM WAS ALSO FAST, independently. It mirrored triso.rs's HEU dispersion (pf 0.30, 1 cm3 box, k~2.08) where neutrons are absorbed long before thermalizing, so the law was never sampled BY CONSTRUCTION and a null result was uninterpretable. Added diagnose_thermal_spectrum_reach (ignored diagnostic, homogenized infinite-medium sweep) to measure this instead of assuming it: 34.41% of 20k fission-born neutrons reach below the 4 eV cutoff after a mean 67.4 scatters. Retuned the case to pf 5e-4 (C/U-235 ~ 3.8e3, order-of-magnitude of a real HTR-10 pebble ~1e4) in a 6 cm reflective cube. Sensitivity is real and was measured: at pf 5e-3 the comparison has no power at all (0.20 sigma).

MEASURED RESULTS (2026-08-14, release, this environment):
  - graphite_thermal_scattering_changes_pebble_bed_keff PASSES. Free-gas C-nat k = 1.08838 +/- 0.01851; bound graphite k = 1.95254 +/- 0.01407; separation 37 sigma (dk = 0.86416, combined sigma 0.02325), 300 particles / 8 inactive + 15 active, ~107 s. Confirming run at 800 particles / 10 + 25: 1.07579 +/- 0.00833 vs 1.94166 +/- 0.00626, 83 sigma, ~410 s. Direction is physically sensible -- the bound law holds a Maxwellian near 0.025 eV where U-235 fission dominates, while the free-gas kernel (stationary target, no up-scatter) lets neutrons slide below thermal into parasitic 1/v capture. This is the gap between a CORRECT and an INCORRECT treatment of the same system, not a design change.
  - MAJORANT RE-CHECK, which this bead's coordinator note explicitly demanded be measured and not assumed (a Woodcock majorant that under-bounds Sigma_t is a SILENT BIAS, not a crash): majorant_still_bounds_total_xs_with_bound_graphite PASSES. Worst Sigma_t/Sigma_maj = 0.909091 over 200k log-spaced points from 1e-4 to 4.2 eV across both materials -- exactly 1/1.1, i.e. the sampling grid captures the true per-bin peak and the entire 10% margin survives even against graphite's 221-edge Bragg sawtooth.
  - Also fixed a latent race in the test helper: the regenerated-tape temp file was named from the PID only, but cargo runs these tests as threads of ONE process, so concurrent callers wrote/read/deleted the same path -- EndfParse("unexpected end of section data"). Now uses a per-call atomic counter. It was invisible while only one test used the helper.

WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH: no benchmark comparison. The reference throughout is this workspace's own njoy port, so these are internal-consistency gates, not an independent NJOY/OpenMC-ACE oracle. The geometry is a packed cube, not HTR-10 -- reproducing HTR-10's published k-effective still needs the real geometry/composition under op-6tz.35 / op-6tz.35.1. AI-assisted draft, human review still owed. Do not describe HTR-10 neutronics as validated on the strength of this.

title: HTR-10 neutronics: graphite S(alpha,beta) end-to-end — no thermal scattering law reaches the pebble-bed transport path at all

description:
FILED 2026-08-11. Two agents landed overlapping mathematics in this crate on the same day; they must be reconciled rather than left as duplicates.

WORK A (op-fm5, landed, uncommitted in tree): every transfer-function block in BOTH tiers now advances by the exact zero-order-hold / step-invariant discrete equivalent, hand-derived per block. Lives in:
  src/lib/alpha_nightly/stable_transfer_functions/{first_order_transfer_fn,first_order_transfer_fn_with_zeroes,second_order_transfer_fn,decaying_sinusoid,decaying_exponentials}.rs
  src/lib/beta_testing/stable_transfer_functions/{same, minus decaying_exponentials}.rs
  verification + O(1) regression tests: */stable_transfer_functions/recurrence_tests.rs
Each carries a module doc deriving Phi = exp(A T), Gamma = integral_0^T exp(A s) ds * B and citing Astrom & Wittenmark, Seborg et al., Franklin/Powell/Workman, Ogata, Hochbruck & Ostermann, Oppenheim & Schafer, and Smith (open access). No editions/years/pages -- none verified against a physical copy, and that constraint should be kept.

WORK B (concurrent, same day): a z_domain module ported from the GNU Octave control package (GPLv3-or-later), including c2d. That is the SAME transformation, generically implemented.

THE QUESTION TO SETTLE: should the hand-derived per-block recurrences call into z_domain::c2d, or stay as they are?
Arguments for keeping them as-is: they are exact closed forms specialised per block (2-3 scalars, no matrix algebra, no allocation), they are what makes the 0.17 us/step figure possible, and they are already verified against the analytic superposition to ~1e-15. Routing them through a general c2d would likely cost performance and would put an Octave-derived GPL port on the hot path of every controller step.
Arguments for reconciling: one source of truth for the discretisation, and z_domain::c2d could be VERIFIED AGAINST the per-block closed forms -- which is probably the real win here, and is cheap: the recurrence_tests.rs analytic-superposition harness can be pointed at c2d output directly.

RECOMMENDED: keep the specialised recurrences on the hot path; add a cross-check test that z_domain::c2d reproduces them for a first-order lag and for all three second-order damping regimes. That gives the shared-truth benefit with no performance cost.

ALSO CHECK: LICENCE PROVENANCE. The crate was relicensed Apache-2.0 -> GPL-3.0-only on 2026-08-11. The op-fm5 recurrences are original work (derived from textbook-standard mathematics, nothing copied) and carry no upstream provenance. The z_domain code IS an Octave port and needs its NOTICE/attribution-header treatment kept intact per the workspace rule. Do not let a later refactor blur which files are which.
title: chem-eng: reconcile the new z_domain c2d port with the ZOH recurrences already in stable_transfer_functions

description:
REVISED 2026-08-13 after maintainer correction. My original framing (fit Gibbs polynomials, write backward equations) was borrowed from the water/IF97 world and was wrong for helium. Corrected framing below.

WHY THE ORIGINAL FRAMING WAS WRONG:
True analytical backward equations exist ONLY for water - the IF97 backend has them because IAPWS-IF97 defines them as a standard. Helium has NO equivalent standard. Upstream CoolProp's substitute is TABULAR INTERPOLATION, and it reaches the same place practically.

VERIFIED IN THIS WORKSPACE 2026-08-13 (grep over crates/outram-park-fork-coolprop/):
  TTSE            0 files
  BICUBIC         0 files
  tabular         0 files
  fast_evaluate   0 files
  AbstractState   0 files
  'backward'      2 files - BOTH are forward/backward SWEEPS in the GAMG and conjugate-gradient linear solvers, i.e. unrelated to thermodynamics.
=> THE FORK IS HEOS-ONLY. It has the accuracy but not the fast path. By the maintainer's own decision rule, this bead STANDS - but as a tabular-backend port, not a polynomial fit.

WHAT TO ACTUALLY BUILD:
  - Port the tabular backends TTSE and BICUBIC. Native inputs are (p,h) and (p,T) - those are fastest because they are what the tables are gridded on. Two table sets get written: pressure-enthalpy and pressure-temperature, cached upstream under HOME/.CoolProp/Tables.
  - Accuracy is essentially free: for R245fa density, BICUBIC matches HEOS to about 9 significant figures.

THE (p,s) CATCH, AND WHERE A HAND-ROLLED RELATION ACTUALLY EARNS ITS KEEP:
(p,s) STILL requires an extra iteration even in the tabular backends, though the overhead is far less severe than the full EOS. And (p,s) is exactly what isentropic turbine and compressor expansion needs in the GTHTR300 Brayton cycle (op-id3l.12). So the one place a bespoke backward relation is justified is the BALANCE OF PLANT, not the core.

TWO PRACTICAL CONSTRAINTS FOR THE PORT:
  1. Table load is 80-140 ms per AbstractState construction. Instantiate ONCE and hold it - in Rust the property object lives in the solver struct, never created per call.
  2. CoolProp 8.0 added fast_evaluate: cache-bypassing, allocation-free batch evaluation writing into a caller-allocated buffer, because the per-call update()/keyed_output() machinery was dominating actual math cost for fast backends. Check which upstream version this fork descends from - an older lineage may have inherited that overhead.

FIRST ACTION IS TO PROFILE, not to write: confirm the per-call overhead is real in our port before choosing between a tabular port and anything bespoke.
title: HTGR Phase 0.2: real-time helium fast path — port CoolProp's TABULAR backends (TTSE/BICUBIC)

description: Port the write side.
